label: Bible Study
prompt: But these are _____, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.
verse: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.
note: John's purpose statement for his whole Gospel — written so you'd believe and live.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: For the LORD thy God hath blessed thee in all the works of thy hand: he knoweth thy walking through this great wilderness: these forty years the LORD thy God hath been with thee; thou hast lacked _____.
verse: For the LORD thy God hath blessed thee in all the works of thy hand: he knoweth thy walking through this great wilderness: these forty years the LORD thy God hath been with thee; thou hast lacked nothing.
note: Forty years in the wilderness, and Moses's summary is two words long: lacked nothing.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the _____? So run, that ye may obtain.
verse: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.
note: Paul borrows from the racetrack: everybody runs, but one gets the prize — so run like you mean it.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Speak unto the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a _____ of blue:
verse: Speak unto the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue:
note: Fringes with a blue cord reminded Israel of God's commands — the woman in Matthew 9 touched Jesus' hem.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: I press toward the _____ for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
verse: I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
note: 'I press toward the mark' — Paul as a runner leaning toward the finish line, eyes off the past.
